And the decisive interaction of the whole lane — Insanity Potion putting Grievous Wounds on Poison Trail, which cuts Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash's drain and World Ender's heal amp together — is absent.

Insanity Potion: 'making his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds'. Aatrox's entire sustain is healing, so anti-heal is the matchup, not stats.

edits.before: Level 1 is Aatrox's only real window — his Darkin Blade Q sweetspot covers surprising range and a knockup stops your run dead, so do not walk directly at him; farm near max Poison Trail range and let him push. At level 2 Fling arrives and you can threaten to toss him into your own minion wave on any overcommit, but his passive healing means one trade still favors him if he catches the knockup. Level 3 is your first decisive moment: drop Mega Adhesive in his path as he steps up for a Q cast, root him when he tries to walk out, and Fling him backward so he spends every remaining second in the poison cloud — the root-fling combo costs him roughly a third of his health bar and he has no dash to escape it.
edits.after: Level 1 is Aatrox's only real window — The Darkin Blade (Q) sweetspot covers surprising range and its knockup stops your run dead, so do not walk straight at him; farm near max Poison Trail range and let him push. His combo opens on a Deathbringer Stance auto-reset, so the wind-up is your cue to step off, not the cast. At level 2 Fling (10s) arrives and you can toss him into your own wave on any overcommit, but his passive healing still wins a stationary trade. Level 3 is your first decisive moment: drop Mega Adhesive (17s) in his path as he steps up, which grounds Umbral Dash so he cannot dash out, then Fling him back into the goo — landing in the adhesive roots him, and he spends every remaining second inside the poison cloud.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a proxy-or-pressure choice: either run behind his tower to eat his wave and deny him CS, or stand at the lane boundary and force him to choose between farming into your poison or backing off and losing tower plates. Aatrox must come to you to farm, which is exactly what Singed wants. At level 6, Insanity Potion changes everything — the armor, magic resistance, AP, and health regeneration stack combine to make you effectively unkillable in the run-past pattern; pop it the moment he activates World Ender R and keep running, because he cannot out-sustain Poison Trail attrition while chasing and your regeneration races his passive during the exchange. Never stop moving into his Q sweetspot zone: keep him chasing the cloud rather than setting up the knockup.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a proxy-or-pressure choice: either run behind his tower to eat his wave and deny him CS, or stand at the lane boundary and force him to choose between farming into your poison or backing off and losing tower plates. Aatrox must come to you to farm, which is exactly what Singed wants. At level 6, Insanity Potion changes everything — not the stat dump but the Grievous Wounds it puts on Poison Trail, which halves Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash's drain and World Ender's heal amp at once; pop it the moment he activates World Ender and keep running, because his whole sustain plan is doing half damage while your regeneration holds. Never stop moving into his Q sweetspot zone: keep him chasing the cloud, and save Mega Adhesive for the step-up so it grounds his dash.
